minutes.headline: Finance Committee heard capital plan deferral questions and agreed to start a debt work group; no budget votes taken.
minutes.summary: The remote meeting opened with public comment on warnings of deep state aid cuts and a dispute over putting free cash into stabilization. The committee then joined the Capital Planning Committee to ask what deferring asbestos abatement, paramedic equipment and other items to a fall town meeting would mean. Members also discussed the streetlight article, a plan for a debt study ahead of big building projects, and how a 1/12th budget would work. The only votes were adjournments.

budget_items.what_was_said: A member relayed a report that Belmont was told to plan on a large local aid cut, and legislators advised planning conservatively.
A member urged putting all free cash into stabilization; the town manager urged reconsidering that recommendation.
The town manager reviewed the projects submitted for state earmarks in February.
Facilities director said the project is out for bid with bids due May 28 and would slip to next July if deferred.
The fire chief noted the equipment spend could occur before a fall town meeting if the money is two million in the hole.
A capital planning member said requests do not go away when deferred and projected future-year requests.
A member noted contractual and step obligations would need to be accounted for in a 1/12th scenario.
Members discussed savings from buying streetlights versus leaving ownership with the utility.
A member suggested a rough ballpark figure for TC Passios borrowing before it goes to town meeting.

decisions.decision: Capital plan recommendation deferred to the next meeting or the June 11 meeting before town meeting.
Next meetings set for May 28 and June 11, with streetlights and debt on the May 28 agenda.
The full committee will begin the debt study on May 28, with members taking pieces of the work and the spreadsheet sent out.
A general town finance and cash flow update was requested for the next meeting.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee took no budget votes; it heard questions on deferring capital items with the Capital Planning Committee, and the capital recommendation was put off.
Members agreed the full committee will begin a debt study on May 28, with pieces of the work divided among members.
Facilities said the asbestos abatement project is out for bid and would slip a year if deferred to a fall town meeting.
Members discussed 1/12th budget obligations, including school step increases, and the savings from buying streetlights from the utility.
Next meetings were set for May 28 and June 11, and a general town finance and cash flow update was requested.

why_it_matters: Deferring capital items to a fall town meeting could delay safety and equipment projects and push their costs into later years, and a debt study ahead of large building projects bears on future borrowing and tax bills.
watch_next: May 28 meeting: streetlight article, start of the debt study, and a town finance and cash flow update.
June 11 meeting before town meeting: the deferred capital plan recommendation.
